Bayesian fit of the fat oxidation curve

Source: R/MFO_bayes.R
MFO_bayes.Rd

Fits the SIN model (Cheneviere et al. 2009) in g/min, or a third-degree polynomial, as a Bayesian model with brms (Burkner 2017, doi:10.18637/jss.v080.i01 ) on Stan (Carpenter et al. 2017, doi:10.18637/jss.v076.i01 ), and returns posterior medians and credible intervals for MFO, Fatmax, the Fatmax zone, Fatmin and the SIN parameters (SPEC 13.2). It does not replace [MFO()]: it is a separate analysis of the steps that [MFO()] returns. brms and rstan are in Suggests.

Usage

MFO_bayes(
  MFO_data,
  model = c("SIN", "P3"),
  priors = NULL,
  sigma = c("constant", "proportional"),
  fatmin_prior = c(90, 14),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 2000,
  conf = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  backend = "rstan",
  adapt_delta = 0.99,
  ...
)

Arguments

MFO_data

the `MFO_db` of an [MFO()] result (columns `porc_VO2` and `FAT`); every row is used, as in [MFO_kinetics()].

model

`"SIN"` (default) or `"P3"`.

priors

optional `brmsprior` object replacing all default priors.

sigma

`"constant"` (default) or `"proportional"` to intensity.

fatmin_prior

mean and SD of the normal prior of Fatmin, truncated to (Fatmax, 100) (default `c(90, 14)`, SIN only).

chains, iter

number of chains and iterations per chain (defaults 4 and 2000, half of them warm-up). With a high Fatmax (trained people) use `iter = 4000`: in simulated tests with Fatmax 64 +/- 8 % VO₂max, 5 of 100 fits had an R-hat above 1.01 with 2000 iterations and none with 4000.

conf

level of the credible intervals (default 0.95).

seed

optional integer passed to Stan.

backend

passed to [brms::brm()] (default `"rstan"`).

adapt_delta

target acceptance rate of the sampler (default 0.99; the SIN likelihood has kinks at the zeros of the curve). Divergent transitions are always reported.

...

further arguments to [brms::brm()].

Value

An object of class `MFO_bayes`: a list with `summary` (one row per quantity: `median`, `lower`, `upper`, `contraction`), `draws` (posterior draws of the parameters and derived quantities), `diagnostics` (maximum R-hat, minimum bulk and tail ESS, divergent transitions, largest posterior correlation among d, s and t), `model`, `sigma`, `conf` and `fit` (the `brmsfit`, e.g. for [brms::loo()]). `plot()` draws posterior curves.

Details

**SIN model.** FAT_i ~ Normal(M sin(min(max(u_i, 0)^s, pi)), sigma), with u = pi^(1/s) / (pi + 2d) (K x + d + t), K = pi / 100 and x in % VO₂max. MFO (M) is a parameter, so there is no normalisation by the highest step. Outside the two zeros of the curve u^s is set to 0 or pi, so fat oxidation is 0 there (as in [simulate_MFO_sessions()]); this also keeps non-integer powers of negative numbers out of Stan (SPEC 13.2).

The model is parametrised by MFO, Fatmax, Fatmin and s, the quantities the data inform; d and t follow from the closed forms of Fatmax and Fatmin (SPEC 6.5) in each draw, with a = 2^(-1/s): t = pi + d - K Fatmin and d = \[pi (1 - a) + K (Fatmax - Fatmin)\] / \[2 (a - 1)\]. The usual parametrisation (d, s, t) has a ridge in the posterior (s and t correlated above 0.9) whose position is set by the priors: with the priors first proposed in SPEC 13.2 (d ~ N(0, 0.3), s ~ LogNormal(0, 0.3), t ~ N(0, 0.2)) the 95 % intervals of s covered the true value in 7-10 % of simulated tests where t is far from 0 (see `vignette("bayes")`). Fatmin is constrained to lie between Fatmax and 100 % VO₂max. The Fatmax zone (FAT >= 90 % of M) also comes from closed forms of each draw.

**P3 model.** FAT ~ b0 + b1 z + b2 z^2 + b3 z^3 with z = (x - 50) / 25; Fatmax, MFO and the zone are found on a grid of the measured intensities for each draw.

**Priors.** The defaults are the authors' weakly informative choices, not estimates from the literature. SIN:

  • M ~ Normal(0.45, 0.25) truncated at 0, centred above the normative mean of sedentary adults (0.34 +/- 0.10 g/min; Amaro-Gahete, Sanchez-Delgado & Ruiz 2018, Front Physiol 9: 1460, Table 1, doi:10.3389/fphys.2018.01460 ) with an inflated SD to cover trained people;

  • Fatmax ~ Normal(50, 15) truncated to (10, 90) % VO₂max, centred between the normative value of sedentary adults (44.2 +/- 12.4; same table) and that of trained men (64 %; Achten, Gleeson & Jeukendrup 2002, doi:10.1097/00005768-200201000-00015 ) with an inflated SD;

  • Fatmin ~ Normal(90, 14) truncated to (Fatmax, 100) % VO₂max (90.1 +/- 14.1 in Cheneviere et al. 2009), set with `fatmin_prior`;

  • s ~ LogNormal(0, 0.3).

P3: b0 ~ Normal(0.3, 0.3), b1-b3 ~ Normal(0, 0.3). sigma ~ Exponential(10) (constant) or, with `sigma = "proportional"`, sigma_i = sigma_100 x_i / 100 with log(sigma_100) ~ Normal(log(0.1), 1). Replace them with `priors` (a `brmsprior` object, e.g. from [brms::prior()]); check them with [MFO_prior_check()].

**Limitation: Fatmax is slightly underestimated.** In simulated tests with s = 1.52 (8 steps, FAT error 5-10 % of MFO) the posterior median of Fatmax was below the truth by a median of 1.1-1.6 % VO₂max, and the 95 % interval missed it in 8-12 of 100 tests, nearly always by underestimation. Part of it comes from the prior of s, centred on a symmetric curve: with s ~ LogNormal(0, 0.5) the bias fell to 0.7-0.9 % VO₂max, but 9-14 % of the fits had divergent transitions, so the default stays LogNormal(0, 0.3). For scale, the typical error of Fatmax with the classical fits in the same tests was 1.6 (5 % noise) and 2.6 (10 %) % VO₂max for the absolute SIN of [MFO_kinetics()] (median absolute error) and 2.5-3.1 and 4.1-5.0 % VO₂max for P3 (RMSE); see `vignette("bayes")` and `vignette("validation")`.

**What to interpret.** `contraction` = 1 - Var(posterior) / Var(prior) tells how much the data narrowed each quantity; below 0.5 it is labelled `prior-dominated` in `print()`. The shape parameters d, s and t are poorly identified among themselves (`print()` gives their largest posterior correlation): interpret MFO, Fatmax and Fatmin, not d, s and t (see [MFO_kinetics()], *What to interpret*).

See also

[MFO_prior_check()], [MFO_kinetics()], [MFO()]

Examples

# Not run: brms compiles a Stan model first (about a minute) and needs a
# C++ toolchain and the headers of rstan (BH, StanHeaders, RcppEigen)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (requireNamespace("brms", quietly = TRUE)) {
  data(list = c("basal_df", "MFO_df", "VO2max_df"), package = "MFO")
  r <- MFO(step_time = 20, db_MFO = MFO_df, db_basal = basal_df,
           db_graded = VO2max_df, cv_var = "RER", author = "Frayn",
           energy_equivalents = "classic", negative_FAT = "keep")
  b <- MFO_bayes(r$MFO_db, seed = 1)
  b
  plot(b)
}
} # }
